prompts.cane-toad:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create a replacement realistic animal icon for a museum-miniature collection chart. Reference image 1 is the existing animal: preserve its species, natural colors and material detail, but REPLACE its frontal/three-quarter view. Reference image 2 (hippopotamus) supplies ONLY the collection's lighting and realistic finish, not anatomy. CRITICAL camera and pose: full-body TRUE LEFT-FACING SIDE ELEVATION, entire animal's long axis parallel to the image plane. Nose at image LEFT, rump at image RIGHT; head and muzzle also in strict side profile, not looking toward the camera, only the near-side eye visible. Long-lens near-orthographic projection with no foreshortening, only very slightly elevated camera so a tiny amount of the back is visible. It is a miniature floating just off a vertical museum wall, invisible shelf just below eye line. Strong soft upper-left/front key light, clear bright upper-left surfaces, darker lower-right relief, very subtle purple reflected fill; strong readable contrast at 128px without black crushed areas. Photoreal anatomically correct animal, natural texture, not a cartoon. Complete silhouette including toes, ears, whiskers and tail with safe clear margins. Center outline on square canvas, longest dimension approximately 92-94% of canvas. Real transparent PNG alpha background. No background color or scenery, no floor, no shelf, no pedestal, no baked cast shadow, no text, labels, border or watermark. No front view, no diagonal or isometric view, no head turned to viewer, no oversized head, no cropped tail or paws.
Subject: a cane toad in a natural compact crouch, clearly seen from its side facing left. Stocky low body, golden-brown rough warty skin, pale cream underside, prominent parotoid gland behind the visible golden eye, blunt snout, bent foreleg and powerful folded hindleg. Four anatomically placed limbs, correct natural toes (four on forefeet, five on hindfeet), far-side limbs partly occluded naturally. Mouth closed. Preserve recognizable toad texture and compact shape. The side of the head and torso must be broadside, not the old diagonally facing pose.
